citation.title: Generative Lattice Units with 3D Diffusion for Inverse Design: GLU3D
citation.authors: Yayati Jadhav; Joeseph Berthel; Chunshan Hu; Rahul Panat; Jack Beuth; Amir Barati Farimani

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The conditional diffusion framework is presented as accelerating lattice design while producing structures with better energy absorption and compression load than conventional unit cells at lower densities.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-to-ML timing ratio is given; Sec. 3 reports 16 h training and approximately 16 s per structure at inference, but no classical runtime comparator.
claim.alternatives: The abstract also claims improved energy absorption and compression load against simple cubic and body-centered-cubic cells at lower densities.

baseline.classical_method: Conventional unit cells (simple cubic and body-centered cubic); classical TO is discussed as motivation but not directly benchmarked
baseline.solver: homogenization / FE analysis described; specific baseline solver not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: Four NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 for training; NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti (12 GB) for inference (Sec. 3)
baseline.ml_time: approximately 16 s per structure, batch size one (Sec. 3)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; training data are generated from 22 TPMS families and hybrid structures (Sec. 2)
baseline.quality_metric: homogenized mechanical properties including stiffness, energy absorption, and maximum compression load; periodicity and mesh generation metrics (Secs. 3-4)
baseline.quality_gap: Abstract reports better energy absorption and compression load at lower density versus simple cubic and body-centered-cubic cells; no numerical gap in abstract.

R1.evidence: Abstract reports faster design and better properties, but no equal-time/equal-quality comparison or classical runtime is presented.

R2.evidence: Secs. 2-3 describe FE homogenization but do not establish an inefficient classical optimization baseline or provide a per-iteration comparison.

R3.evidence: Sec. 3 reports 16 h training and approximately 16 s inference per design; Sec. 2 describes training-data construction but gives no data-generation cost or break-even uses.

R4.evidence: Secs. 3-4 evaluate generated geometries and report successful mesh-yield percentages (Table 1), but do not report the rate of designs failing target-property or other physical constraints.

reporting.n_test_cases: not stated (22 TPMS structure families reported in Sec. 2)

notes: The abstract's speed claim is not quantified against a classical optimizer. Public code is linked in the article (reference 100), but no license or complete runnable benchmark information was established for retest eligibility.
